title: ALPS-ADR Mapping
description: Maps ALPS Section 7 features to the ADRs that record their decisions, organized by DDD bounded context (top-level category key) and feature/vertical-slice (optional second segment). Carries an optional advisory subdomainType (core/supporting/generic) overlay per context. The link between an ADR and the code that implements it is not stored here — agents locate the relevant code by reading the ADR and searching the repo. Note: draft-07 cannot express the dependsOn cross-entry invariants (references an existing key, no self-edge, acyclic) — those are enforced by scripts/adr-structure-lint.mjs (R16) and adr-sync step 6, not this schema.

$schema.description: Optional JSON Schema pointer; ignored by the tools but allowed so editors can resolve validation.

alpsDocument.description: Path to the ALPS .alps.xml file relative to the repo root.

categories.description: Map of category id (kebab-case) to mapping entry. Category id matches the ADR directory path under docs/adr/. The top segment is a DDD bounded context / subdomain named with the domain expert's ubiquitous-language term (e.g., 'identity', 'ordering'); the optional second segment is a user-perceived feature / vertical slice (e.g., 'identity/login'). At most two segments — no deeper nesting; the propertyNames.pattern enforces the ≤2-kebab-segment shape so a 3-segment key ('identity/login/social') or an uppercase key ('F1') is rejected at validation time, not just in prose. When a context holds exactly one feature the second segment is elided and a single-segment key means context==feature (legacy/flat layout, e.g. 'auth'). Keys are derived from the feature NAME, never from a PRD Feature ID — the id is preserved in 'alpsFeatureId' instead, so '/adr-impl f1' matches via that field and the folder need not be named 'f1'. Only when no meaningful kebab name exists (e.g. a purely numeric workshop id) is the id used as a fallback single-segment key. See structure.md '디렉토리 구조' and 'ALPS ↔ ADR 매핑'.

feature.description: Human-readable feature name from ALPS Section 7 (for feature-level entries) or the bounded-context name (for context-level entries).

alpsFeatureId.description: Stable id of the feature in the ALPS document (e.g., F-LOGIN-01). This is where the PRD Feature ID lives — the category KEY is derived from the feature name, not this id, so '/adr-impl f1' resolves by matching this field. Populated by feature-to-adr from ALPS Section 7; omit when there is no ALPS PRD.

subdomainType.description: DDD subdomain classification of the bounded context this category belongs to. Advisory metadata only — never a hard gate and never a folder tier. Feature contexts are typically core/supporting; system-wide cross-cutting contexts (infra/integration/security/platform/data) are generic. Place it on the context-level entry (the top-folder entry, or a single-feature flat entry); per-feature sub-folder entries inherit the parent context's type conceptually and may omit it. Surfaced by adr-sync and the hook snapshot as advisory context (e.g. grouping by domain, 'generic — candidate for off-the-shelf'), never enforced. Omit when unknown.

adrs.description: Paths to ADR markdown files (relative to repo root), each listed exactly once across the whole file. MAY be empty ([]) for a context-level grouping entry that holds no context-direct (cross-cutting) ADR — its feature sub-folder entries carry the actual ADRs (e.g. an 'identity' entry with adrs:[] alongside 'identity/login' and 'identity/signup'). Feature/flat entries normally have at least one path. adr-sync step 6 additionally requires every on-disk NNNN-*.md to appear here exactly once and every path here to resolve on disk.

dependsOn.description: Category ids this category depends on (prerequisites). Sourced from the ALPS Section 6.3 Feature Dependency Diagram by feature-to-adr (edge 'this --depends on--> X' becomes X in this list), or recorded directly by adr-new when the author names a prerequisite ADR. Read by adr-impl to implement prerequisite ADRs first, and validated by adr-sync. Uses the same key namespace as 'categories' (single-segment or two-segment context/feature keys). Edges MAY cross bounded-context boundaries (e.g. an ordering/checkout feature depending on an identity/login feature is a normal DDD context relationship). Must reference existing category keys; keep acyclic (no self-edge).

tableDocs.description: Paths to schema/table documents (e.g., docs/tables/*.md, prisma/schema.prisma) that must stay bidirectionally linked with ADRs in this category. Used by the authoring-rules DB schema co-change rule and by adr-sync auxiliary doc check.
